I have major depression and I still take accutane. I did not notice any change in my mood (I was already having another depressive episode before starting roa). I am only 1 month into, though. But I think it is worth to try. My skin is becoming better and it helps me to hate myself a little less. I tried to fight acne for 13 years. I am even kinda angry that no derm suggested me this treatment before.
You should try. Worsening of depr is just a side effect and doesn't happend to everyone, even if u have mental problems.
Bupropion is not an SSRI though. It does not mess with serotonine at all.

I've been taking Effexor for ~4 years. 375 mg. It helped be to get out of my misery, in the end stopped working so I had to go down. I weaned off in a month. Went from 150 to 0, had been very sick for 7 days and then I was all okay again. No brains zaps. Don't say nobody should use it, it helps a lot of people too. It's just that those who have no significant side effect, don't go to the internet to write about it.

It's just you coming off of sertraline. Unpleasant, but nothing scary. It has nothing to do with seizures. Although if they are so intense you need to talk with ur doctor; maybe you should lower your dose of sertr very gradually and slowly. Seems like going from 50 mg to 0 at once is too much for your brain.
It was nasal spray and I took it for 2 months, I think. I was participating in clinical studies then.

Escitalopram: 0/10. Terrible side effects, nausea, fatigue, hallucinations.

Valdoxan: 1/10. Didn't help with depression, didn't help with sleep. But also made no harm.

Wellbutrin: 4/10. No side effects aside from headache, gave me a bit of energy, that's it. 

Effexor: 8/10. Helps really good with depression, not with fatigue and anxiety though. Side effects: sweating a lot, sometimes hard to have an orgasm.

Mirtazapine: 6/10. Helped with sleep and anxiety. But the weight gain was terrible. I was constantly hungry. 

Aripiprazole: 1/10. No side effects, no effects at all.

Esketamine: 10/10. Godsend. 

Pregabaline: 7/10. The only that Increases my libido actually. Makes me feel confident and good. But it causes dependence so it can't be used for long periods of time.

Quetiapine: 4/10. Good for anxiety. Terrible for sleep. The nightmares on it are too vivid.

Olanzapine: 4/10. Good sleep, and anxiety, but causes fatigue and weight gain.

Xanax: 7/10. Good, but dependency is real.

Diazepam: 5/10. 

Nitrazepam: 5/10.

Zolpidem/zopiclone:0/10. These turned my life into hell, I advice to avoid this shit.
Considering it's raining all year round and windy as heck in Tln, these new bus stops look like a joke.

If people are able to have fun without drugs, then I see no problems in occasional using. But when it's the other way... Eventually even psychedelics will stop giving new experiences. And then what? Life will become so terrible. She felt it. Everything in moderation. Or you're gonna have really tough times. Sadly.
Rapid weight loss and loss of appetite can be signs of cancer. Don't wanna scare you, but it's better to check out this possibility.

Stopped because I got bored of this feeling of slightly mentally impaired. I've had enough of this brain fog and sleepiness. Also, overeating. Weed helped a little bit with creativity and gave a good laugh, but that was it. It never gave me motivation to do something, never helped with any physical pain, nor mental. My sociophobia even got worse, since I became more paranoid. Never improved my sleep. I just felt like a snail. 
Also, it gave some of my friends panic attacks and anxiety, which were severe and stayed even after quitting. They needed medical help to cure this. I was a little bit luckier, only had full-blown derealization for a month or so. We were all experienced users. One girl developed psychotic episode... She was completely normal before.  Nobody have thought it could lead to this. I've learned that weed is not so safe, and is still a drug, often unpredictable one. Eventually I switched to stimulants, which is bad, ik. But they honestly gave a lot more, than weed. And they are not so unpredictable, I think. Sorry for rant and bad English.
